title: AuroraCloud x Redwood - Marketplace & Reference Architecture Tech Sync
summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for AuroraCloud marketplace tile, and joint solution integration plan. Discussed onboarding checklist, SSO/KMS/Network considerations, benchmark plan for performance profiles, and next steps for docs and pilot. Agreed to run a staging listing and a small pilot in Q4.
topics: Integration for dedicated vs hosted models
next_steps: Redwood to share marketplace checklist & packaging guide (Sam) by 2026-10-02
Aurora to provision test tenant and grant Redwood staging access (Priya) by 2026-10-06
SEs to align on benchmark plan and dataset (Marisol + Luis) by 2026-10-09
Schedule follow-up 30-minute pilot kickoff the week of 2026-10-12
action_items: Sam Patel: share marketplace asset checklist and publisher contact info; due 2026-10-02
Priya Sinha: provision Aurora staging tenant, grant IAM roles for Redwood; due 2026-10-06
Marisol Chen & Luis Ortega: define benchmark scenarios (latency p95, throughput, cost/cycle); due 2026-10-09
Jordan Kim: draft reference architecture doc outline; due 2026-10-05
transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2026-09-25 08:00 PT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Sam (Redwood AE), Marisol (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood Product), Ava (Redwood Partnerships); Priya (Aurora PM), Luis (Aurora Cloud Architect), Marta (Aurora Marketplace Ops), Kenji (Aurora Security)

[00:00] Sam: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Priya: yep loud and clear, thanks Sam.
[00:06] Marisol: good morning afternoon depending where you are, we'll try to keep to the agenda - marketplace listing, ref arch, and a pilot plan.
[00:15] Luis: quick note from our side, we're trying to get a marketplace tile live by end of Q4 so timeline is kinda compressed.
[00:20] Jordan: great, that's useful context; we want to make sure the technical bits don't add surprises.
[00:28] Marta: can we start with what exact assets you need from us for the listing? last time the doc had a lot of fields and some of the screenshots are tricky because of our UI.
[00:35] Sam: totally, I'll run through the checklist we use - publisher logo, short and long descriptions, billing integration details, a reference architecture diagram, deploy scripts or helm charts for private/managed deployments, plus any compliance badges like SOC2. we'll send the checklist after.
[00:48] Priya: perfect. on billing, we need to know if Redwood will handle subscription billing for a managed offering or if Aurora expects to resell with our own billing.
[00:55] Ava: short answer: we support both patterns; for marketplace listing we can be the publisher and Redwood can handle metering/costing, or we can co-list and you manage billing. decision impacts the integration flow.
[01:10] Kenji: security question - for private deployments we require KMS integration and audit logs. does Redwood support customer-managed keys?
[01:16] Marisol: yes, we support KMS/HSM via our Private deployments; that works for both VPC and on-prem options. sometimes the transcription later calls it "Redwood Privet" in the logs, sorry.
[01:26] Luis: and for network, do you have guidance on VPC peering vs private link? what's your recommended pattern for low latency to the inference endpoints?
[01:34] Marisol: we recommend Private Link or direct peering for lowest latency; VPC peering is fine but cross-account routing can complicate things. we'll include a reference architecture diagram that shows both patterns and notes on route tables, security groups and NAT.
[01:46] Marta: will that diagram be a vendor neutral doc or specific to Aurora's infra?
[01:50] Jordan: we'll provide a general ref-arch plus a sample tuned to Aurora if you share your account space and some details, like whether you're using GKE or EKS or Aurora's managed k8s.
[02:00] Priya: we're on EKS and also run some on-prem Kubes for regulated customers. the tile needs to show both marketplace quick start for hosted and instructions for private deployment.
[02:09] Sam: noted. next up - the technical listing requirements for the marketplace UI: a 300x300 icon, short blurb, long description, launch flow (launch in marketplace -> provision in your account vs redirect to Redwood hosted).
[02:24] Luis: on the launch flow, can we support a guided provisioning where customer chooses hosted vs dedicated during install?
[02:30] Marisol: yes, our Marketplace integration supports a parameterized launch that can kick off either a Redwood Hosted subscription, or deploy a Helm chart into the customer's cluster for private. there are some permission requirements for the latter - cluster-admin-ish permissions to create service accounts, CRDs, etc.
[02:45] Kenji: about permissions, we need to ensure least privilege. can you provide an RBAC manifest that limits scope?
[02:49] Marisol: we'll produce RBAC templates and a minimal set of IAM roles. in practice some operators need elevated rights during install, but we document rollback and how to scope them.
[03:00] Priya: ok. next is the reference arch doc - Jordan, can you walk through the high level components you'd expect in the Aurora doc?
[03:05] Jordan: sure. top level: 1) network topology options (private link / peering), 2) identity & auth (SSO/SAML, service accounts), 3) encryption (KMS for user data, in-transit TLS), 4) runtime options (Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, Private), 5) deployment artifacts (helm chart, container images, manifest examples), 6) monitoring & cost controls (token-level cost breakdown hooks and batching settings).
[03:27] Luis: for monitoring, we need to integrate with Aurora's observability - do you emit Prometheus metrics or a tracing endpoint?
[03:32] Marisol: yes, we expose Prometheus metrics, a few tracing hooks for Jaeger/OTel, and logs can be shipped to your logging pipeline. we also have endpoints for per-route latency/cost spikes.
[03:44] Marta: do you provide a sandbox or demo environment we can spin up for Marketplace QA?
[03:48] Sam: we have a Redwood staging tenant for partners. Sam: we'll ask partnerships to invite Aurora to staging and give test credentials - that's in the action items.
[03:57] Priya: great. on benchmarks - we want a concise test plan so our cert team can validate performance. what metrics do you recommend?
[04:04] Marisol: p95 latency for 512 tokens, throughput at 8 concurrent sessions, memory/cpu usage, and cost per 1k tokens at the configured quantization. also cold-start times for dedicated pools. we'll draft a spreadsheet for you.
[04:18] Luis: can we run those tests against a small dedicated pool to mirror production? we'd like the pilot to exercise the Dedicated mode since that's what some customers will buy.
[04:27] Marisol: yep we can provision a small Dedicated pool for the pilot. note there's a lead time to spin up GPU capacity in some regions; we should pick a region early.
[04:38] Priya: Aurora prefers US-east-1 for the initial pilot.
[04:41] Sam: we'll plan for that.
[04:44] Marta: any compliance artifacts we should include in the listing? we need to show SOC2 type II or at least an attestation.
[04:51] Ava: Redwood can share SOC2 report and ISO summary under an NDA; we'll add that to the checklist for the marketplace tile.
[04:58] Kenji: KMS flow detail: how do you handle envelope encryption? who has access to plaintext in the hosted flow?
[05:05] Marisol: for hosted we use envelope encryption with customer-managed keys when requested; Redwood operators do not get plaintext access when CMK is enabled. for private deployments you're fully in control. we'll add a KMS appendix.
[05:17] Priya: excellent. on marketing, do you want a joint solution brief and maybe a co-hosted webinar once the marketplace tile is live?
[05:24] Ava: yes, joint brief and a short reference architecture walkthrough webinar is high value. we can coordinate PR/launch timing after the pilot.
[05:31] Jordan: also we should capture a small customer-facing diagram for the listing page that shows quick install vs managed flow.
[05:36] Luis: back to integrations - how do you handle fallback when Dedicated pool is saturated? is there automatic routing to hosted cheaper variant?
[05:44] Marisol: Redwood has smart routing and fallback policies; we can route requests between capacity tiers and to compatible model variants. there's a policy layer in config for per-tenant fallbacks. note: the transcriber often munges "KV cache" into "KV cash" in older notes.
[05:59] Priya: ok noted. we need to include that behavior in the listing so customers understand SLA differences.
[06:05] Sam: good point. we'll include an SLA table mapping Dedicated SLA, Hosted SLOs, and fallback behaviors.
[06:12] Marta: timeline recap? you mentioned end of Q4 for listing live. can you propose milestones?
[06:18] Sam: proposed milestones: 1) asset & checklist ready (Oct 2), 2) staging tenant & RBAC (Oct 6), 3) ref-arch draft (Oct 5), 4) benchmark plan (Oct 9), 5) pilot run (Mid Oct), 6) listing QA and certification (late Oct/early Nov).
[06:36] Priya: that timeline works for us but final certification depends on pilot results.
[06:41] Marisol: on pilot scope - we'll run a 1-week benchmark suite plus a few end-to-end installs in your staging. please highlight any special security constraints for the pilot.
[06:52] Kenji: for pilot, Aurora requires that no customer data is used; we'll provide synthetic prompt sets. also need an audit log export at the end.
[07:01] Marisol: fine. we'll use synthetic test data and enable audit logging; we'll provide an export.
[07:06] Priya: are there any gotchas with the marketplace cert process you've seen before?
[07:11] Sam: often the small things slow review: 1) missing RBAC least-privilege manifest, 2) no clear rollback plan for helm installs, 3) unclear billing flow if you want resale. we'll preempt those.
[07:25] Marta: about billing again - can you share a sample billing payload and metering events schema? our billing team needs that to wire into Aurora marketplace.
[07:33] Marisol: yes we'll share metering schema and example events.
[07:37] Luis: for the reference arch doc can you include example terraform snippets for networking and security groups? that helps our infra team.
[07:45] Jordan: absolutely - we'll include terraform and helm snippets; also a minimal manifest for the operator.
[07:52] Priya: one last ask - can we have a short checklist for the marketplace cert team that summarizes steps they need to validate?
[07:58] Sam: yes we'll add a Marketplace QA checklist to the assets.
[08:02] Ava: ok quick recap of owners and dates then we'll open for any final questions - Sam?
[08:08] Sam: recap: Sam share checklist & assets by 2026-10-02; Jordan draft ref-arch outline by 2026-10-05; Marisol + Luis define benchmark plan by 2026-10-09; Priya to provision staging by 2026-10-06. schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-10-12.
[08:25] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:27] Luis: thanks, appreciate it.
[08:28] Marta: thanks all.
[08:29] Kenji: bye.
[08:30] Sam: bye everyone, sending notes and assets after the call.

End of transcript
